OpenGL mobject classes

Source: R/zz_opengl_mobjects.R
opengl_mobjects.Rd

Upstream's OpenGL renderer has its own mobject classes, such as OpenGLCircle or OpenGLVGroup. manimR draws every mobject with grid, so each of them is a subclass of its Cairo counterpart that takes the same arguments: OpenGLCircle() is a Circle() and inherits(x, "OpenGLCircle") is TRUE. Code written for the OpenGL renderer runs unchanged; the GPU pipeline itself (shaders, the OpenGL camera and window) is not part of manimR.

Arguments

uv_surface

A Surface().

resolution

Number of mesh lines along u and v.

stroke_width

Width of the mesh lines.

normal_nudge

Distance the mesh is moved along the surface normal.

depth_test, flat_stroke, shader_folder

Settings of upstream's shaders, kept but not used.

image_file

Image file (looked up with get_full_raster_image_path()) or array for the texture.

dark_image_file

Image for the dark side, stored in dark_image.

image_mode

Mode the image is converted to, as in ImageMobject().

...

Further arguments for VGroup() or Surface().

Value

A mobject: an R6 object of the class named by the function called. The objects whose names end in Class are the R6 class generators that these functions call.

Details

Three classes have no Cairo counterpart:

  • OpenGLSurfaceGroup(...) is a surface without faces of its own that holds the surfaces it is given.

  • OpenGLSurfaceMesh(uv_surface) is a VGroup() of curves along the grid lines of a surface (resolution lines in each direction, 21 by default), lifted normal_nudge along the surface normal so they show on top of it.

  • OpenGLTexturedSurface(uv_surface, image_file) is a copy of a surface whose faces take the color of the image at their center: u runs along the image from left to right and v from bottom to top, as upstream's texture coordinates. Upstream's shader shows dark_image_file on the side facing away from the light; manimR keeps it in dark_image but draws the light image on both sides.

Examples

c1 <- OpenGLCircle(radius = 2)
inherits(c1, "Circle")
#> [1] TRUE
s <- OpenGLSurface(function(u, v) c(u, v, u * v), u_range = c(-1, 1), v_range = c(-1, 1),
                   resolution = 8)
mesh <- OpenGLSurfaceMesh(s, resolution = c(5, 5))
length(mesh$submobjects)
#> [1] 10
img <- matrix(c("red", "blue", "green", "white"), 2, 2)
tex <- OpenGLTexturedSurface(s, img)
